`driverName` here is `reflect.TypeOf(c.Driver()).String()` — a Go type name
like `*stdlib.Driver` or `*mysql.MySQLDriver`. `ParseDSN`'s registry
(`dsnparse/parse.go:103-121`) and the `db.system.name` switch in
`semconv/db.go:56-71` are both keyed by registered driver-name strings
(`"pgx"`, `"mysql"`, ...), which a reflected type name never matches.

Concretely, for the two drivers named in this PR's own motivation:
- `pgx/v5/stdlib` → `driverName = "*stdlib.Driver"` → falls to
  `bestEffortParse` (URL-only) and `db.system.name` becomes `other_sql`
  instead of `postgresql`.
- `go-sql-driver/mysql` `NewConnector` → `*mysql.MySQLDriver` → not in the
  registry, and `bestEffortParse` can't parse the non-URL
  `user:pass@tcp(host:3306)/db` form → `addr` stays `"unknown"`.

So this reintroduces the exact `server.address: "unknown"` bug the PR sets
out to fix, for the connectors it explicitly targets, and additionally
degrades `db.system.name` for every `OpenDB` caller. The driver name needs
to be resolved to the registered name (e.g. by matching `c.Driver()`
against the drivers registered via `sql.Register`/`sql.Drivers()`) rather
than derived from the Go type.

`DSN()`/`DataSourceName()` aren't part of `driver.Connector`; they're
probed structurally. Neither `go-sql-driver/mysql`'s connector nor
`pgx/v5/stdlib`'s connector implements either method, so for the drivers
this PR is meant to cover, `dsn` stays `""` here in practice — the fallback
below (`ParseDSN`/`ParseDbName`) never gets real input regardless of the
driver-name fix in the previous comment.

Worth confirming: which connector implementations in the ecosystem actually
expose `DSN()`/`DataSourceName()`? If it's a small minority, it's worth
saying so in the PR description so reviewers know this covers a narrower
slice of "connector-based init" than the motivation implies.

consistency?

mapping a `driver.Driver` instance back to its registered name — e.g.

ParseSnippet builds its wrapper as "package main; func _() {" + source + "}" with no newline before the closing brace, whereas the code being replaced here wrapped with "...\n}\n". Since ImportAliasMap feeds the type matching in apply_call.go, apply_directive.go, apply_lit.go and shared.go, a wrong resolution here means a rule can silently match against the wrong package's type.

Would probably want to track "this alias is ambiguous" as its own state rather than deleting the map entry, so a later collision doesn't un-ambiguous it by accident.
